Higher rankings (a low numerical value) indicate better, usually simpler, regulations for businesses and stronger protections of property rights.Limitations of the indicator: Besides its exclusive focus on the cost of regulation and not on the quality (with the consequent risk of promoting deregulation) and its risks for distorting policy priorities ( promotes the focus of governments on climbing in the ranking rather than in reforming their business environment), the methodological weaknesses are even more pronounced in the context of SubSaharan Africa, in which the number of reliable data contributors is very limited.
